During Ewing's second season, the team started with a 4–12 record and head coach Hubie Brown was dismissed in favor of assistant [Bob Hill](/wiki/Bob_Hill "Bob Hill").[[57]](#cite_note-57) Under Hill, the Knicks had brief successes but went on to lose seventeen of their twenty-one final games of the season to finish 20–46 under Hill and 24–58 on the season.[[58]](#cite_note-58)[[59]](#cite_note-59) Hill was dismissed at season's end.[[60]](#cite_note-Pitino_turnaround-60)

2021 Atlanta Braves season :: Regular season :: chunk_0001
The 2021 season wasn't a smooth sailing road for the [Atlanta Braves](/wiki/Atlanta_Braves "Atlanta Braves"). The Braves started off 0-4 and ended April with a 12–14 record. At the All-Star Break they were 44–45.[[5]](#cite_note-2021Braves-6) After the All-Star Break in August they started ramping it up and went 18–8. On August 8, they climbed over .500 for the first time, at 57–56, and on Aug 15. they took over first place in the NL East, ending up winning the NL East with a 88–73 record.[[5]](#cite_note-2021Braves-6)

The team's turnaround began after July 10 when [Ronald Acuña Jr.](/wiki/Ronald_Acu%C3%B1a_Jr. "Ronald Acuña Jr.") suffered a season ending injury and the [trade deadline](/wiki/Trade_deadline "Trade deadline") approached.[[6]](#cite_note-Braves2021-7) After the Braves' star outfielder got injured, GM [Alex Anthopoulos](/wiki/Alex_Anthopoulos "Alex Anthopoulos") remade his outfield by bringing in veterans [Adam Duvall](/wiki/Adam_Duvall "Adam Duvall"), [Joc Pederson](/wiki/Joc_Pederson "Joc Pederson"), [Eddie Rosario](/wiki/Eddie_Rosario "Eddie Rosario"), and [Jorge Soler](/wiki/Jorge_Soler "Jorge Soler"). They made a huge impact on the team with Duvall finishing the season with a National League-leading 113 [RBIs](/wiki/Run_batted_in "Run batted in") (45 with the Braves); Pederson hit a game-winning home run in the [NLDS](/wiki/NLDS "NLDS") against the [Brewers](/wiki/Milwaukee_Brewers "Milwaukee Brewers"); Rosario was the NLCS MVP; Soler was the [World Series](/wiki/World_Series "World Series") MVP.[[6]](#cite_note-Braves2021-7)

University of Rostock :: History :: 1419–1919 :: chunk_0001
The university was founded in 1419 by confirmation of [Pope Martin V](/wiki/Pope_Martin_V "Pope Martin V") and thus is one of the oldest universities in Northern Europe.

In Germany, there are only five universities that were founded earlier, while only Heidelberg and Leipzig operated continuously since then: [Heidelberg](/wiki/University_of_Heidelberg "University of Heidelberg") (1386), [Cologne](/wiki/University_of_Cologne "University of Cologne") (1388/1919), [Erfurt](/wiki/University_of_Erfurt "University of Erfurt") (1392/1994), [Würzburg](/wiki/University_of_W%C3%BCrzburg "University of Würzburg") (1402/1582) and [Leipzig](/wiki/University_of_Leipzig "University of Leipzig") (1409).
That makes Rostock University the third oldest German university in continuous operation.

Throughout the 15th and 16th centuries, the University of Rostock had about 400 to 500 students each year and was among the most important universities in Germany and Northern Europe at the time, with many of its students originating from the [Low Countries](/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries"), [Scandinavia](/wiki/Scandinavia "Scandinavia") or other countries bordering the [Baltic Sea](/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea").

In the course of political struggles and due to pressure from the church, the university moved to [Greifswald](/wiki/Greifswald "Greifswald") in 1437 and remained there until 1443. From 1487 to 1488 teaching took place in [Lübeck](/wiki/L%C3%BCbeck "Lübeck"). A few years after the city of Rostock, the university became [Protestant](/wiki/Protestant "Protestant") in 1542. Henceforth, [Humanism](/wiki/Humanism "Humanism") and [Lutheranism](/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism") were defining characteristics of the university.

In the 16th century, Rostock was the first university to teach [Copernicanism](/wiki/Copernicanism "Copernicanism"), which was introduced by Professor [Duncan Liddel](/wiki/Duncan_Liddel "Duncan Liddel")

After the Soviets launched [Sputnik](/wiki/Sputnik "Sputnik"), von Braun promoted a plan for the US Army to establish a military lunar outpost by 1965.

Alcohol consumption at any [quantity](/wiki/Quantity "Quantity") is a risk factor for [head and neck cancers](/wiki/Head_and_neck_cancer "Head and neck cancer"), such as cancers of the [mouth](/wiki/Oral_cancer "Oral cancer"), [esophagus](/wiki/Esophageal_cancer "Esophageal cancer"), [pharynx](/wiki/Pharyngeal_cancer "Pharyngeal cancer") and [larynx](/wiki/Laryngeal_cancer "Laryngeal cancer").[[48]](#cite_note-:6-48)

The U.S. [National Cancer Institute](/wiki/National_Cancer_Institute "National Cancer Institute") states "Drinking alcohol increases the risk of cancers of the mouth, esophagus, pharynx, larynx, and liver in men and women, … In general, risks increases above baseline with any alcohol intake (mild; <2 glass of wine per week) and increases significantly with moderate alcohol intake (one glass of wine per day) with highest risk in those with greater than 7 glasses of wine per week. (A drink is defined as 12 ounces of regular beer, 5 ounces of wine, or 1.5 ounces of 80-proof liquor.) … Also, using alcohol with [tobacco](/wiki/Tobacco "Tobacco") is riskier than using either one alone, because it further increases the chances of getting cancers of the mouth, throat, and esophagus."
